source.title: Generalizing Similarity in Noisy Setups: The DIBS Phenomenon

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. Some equations and figure text are imperfectly extracted, but the results relevant to the claim are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps network width and measures test error, directly testing model-wise double descent with the same kind of intervention and measure, in Siamese similarity-learning settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-width sweeps and their test-error outcomes. It also discusses online/offline comparisons and cited double-descent findings, but those do not test whether more data raises test error near the interpolation threshold; cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Width sweeps of Siamese MLP/CNN branches measuring test error across width, under clean and noisy labels. This is the model-wise double-descent protocol applied to a new setting (similarity learning), so T3 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Additions: the authors stress that double descent appears in SNNs even without noise, unlike typical classification. They also find that the online/offline correspondence holds only for clean data and breaks under label noise in all settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses width sweeps and test-error measurements to examine double descent, but applies them to Siamese similarity learning with pair-density scenarios and two noise constructions rather than the original supervised classification or regression settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Pair density and noise type affect the curves: sparse PLN and SLN behave similarly, while dense PLN shifts the peak rightward and leaves higher overparameterized test error. Increasing noise worsens test error but does not significantly shift the peak.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing the noise amount does not significantly shift the double-descent peak location along width, while noise type under dense pairs (PLN vs SLN) does shift it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Peak location along model size is insensitive to label-noise rate but depends on noise structure and data density.

fits_no_version.finding: Under dense PLN, the asymptotic training error is bounded away from zero and matches the Theorem 1 bounds (Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inconsistent pair labels prevent interpolation regardless of model size.

record.problems: The authors describe the work as exploratory and do not provide quantitative results about the interpolation threshold. Several relevant model-width outcomes are presented qualitatively or in figures. The study does not test epoch-wise double descent, regularization, or sample-wise double descent.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Online/offline comparisons in Figure 6 were not included because they do not test whether more samples raise test error near the interpolation threshold.

untested.parts: Only Siamese MLP/CNN similarity learning on MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR10 with 6000 training pairs; no other architectures or tasks.
Epoch-wise double descent is explicitly not investigated (Limitations).
Sample-wise double descent is not investigated. The online/offline comparison fixes weight updates and does not sweep samples near the threshold.
No effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested.
Variance as the cause, multiple descent, and optimal regularization are not tested; regularization is excluded in Limitations.

missing.what: SLN test error is higher than PLN at small-to-medium widths, while PLN is higher in the deep overparameterized regime. This is a noise-type effect on the shape of the curve.
missing.locator: Section 3, DD results, paragraph after peak-shift discussion; Fig. 1 bottom

missing.what: Per-setup peak locations (npl or k) and average overparameterized test errors for no-noise, SLN and PLN under S1/S2. These are in the figure only, so the numbers are not readable from the text.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T1 to T3 because similarity learning is a new setting. The record's V6 'challenges' label on r1 is downgraded to limits_scope: noise is unnecessary here but still amplifies the peak. The record's V6 label on r5 is removed, since no version claims that the peak shifts with noise amount. All results are qualitative in the text, with numbers only in figures.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests Siamese networks on its stated datasets and setups, not model-wise double descent across all deep-network architectures or tasks.
The authors explicitly state that epoch-wise double descent is not investigated.
The online/offline comparisons vary dataset size, but do not test whether increasing sample size near the interpolation threshold raises test error.
Only Siamese neural networks are tested; the study does not test the claim across different model classes.
The study does not propose or test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across size, epochs, and samples.
The study varies label-noise type and amount and reports whether double descent occurs, but does not test variance as the cause, triple or multiple descent, or optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that transforms the curve into an ordinary U-shape.
